newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy could change VAT bands this year - Visco.
newsitem.headline: Italy could change VAT bands this year - Visco.

text.p: Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco said Italy might introduce a change to Italian value added tax (VAT) bands before the end of the year, adding that the alterations would depend on how inflation performs.
Under a European Union directive, Italy must scrap its four percent VAT and make five percent the lowest level. It must also make some alterations to the upper levels of VAT.
Newspapers have reported that the government is considering including the changes in the 1998 budget, which has to be approved by year-end, to raise money for next year.
"We might do it before the budget, with the budget or even after the budget," Visco told reporters. "I'm not thinking of introducing it tomorrow or next month, but..."
He added that the "performance of inflation" would be instrumental in deciding what changes to introduce and when they would be made.
Visco said he expected the 1998 budget would include deficit cuts of no more than one percent of gross domestic product -- the equivalent of around 20 trillion lire.
